entities.name: PMID:25092560
observations: Prospective single-center study of 154 subjects screened to exclude pathological constipation or incontinence; mean age 59.1 years.
Men had longer anal sphincter length (4.23 vs 3.85 cm; p<0.001) and higher maximum squeeze pressure (190.18 vs 116.49 mmHg; p<0.001); maximum resting pressure did not differ by gender (p=0.93).

Anal sphincter length did not correlate with age (p=0.707); resting pressure declined with age in both sexes (men R²=0.152, women R²=0.282; both p<0.001); squeeze pressure declined with age in women only (R²=0.210; p<0.001).

entities.name: Age-sex manometry effects
observations: In a prospective normal-bowel-function cohort, gender and age related to some—but not all—anorectal manometry measures; effects were parameter-specific.
